Healthcare: Ransomware and double-extortion remain the dominant threat to care delivery, with EHR downtime directly impacting patient safety.
Legacy and unmanaged medical / IoT devices expand the attack surface beyond traditional endpoints.
Commodity infostealers harvest credentials that feed targeted intrusions into clinical systems.
Finance: Banking trojans and infostealers target credential theft and fraudulent transfers.
Supply-chain and third-party fintech integrations broaden exposure.
Regulatory pressure (PCI, GLBA) raises the cost of dwell time and undetected lateral movement.
Retail: POS malware and web-skimming (Magecart-style) target cardholder data at scale.
Seasonal traffic spikes are exploited to hide malicious activity in the noise.
Botnet / credential-stuffing pressure on customer accounts and loyalty programs.
Critical Infrastructure: State-aligned actors probe OT / ICS environments for pre-positioning.
IT / OT convergence lets commodity malware reach operational networks.
Manufacturing: Ransomware against production lines causes outsized operational and revenue impact.
IP theft via RATs and infostealers targets designs and process data.
Flat OT networks accelerate lateral movement once a foothold exists.
Government: Nation-state espionage and credential harvesting target sensitive data.
Legacy systems and constrained budgets slow patch and detection cycles.
Supply-chain compromise is a recurring intrusion vector.
Technology: Source-code and CI/CD pipelines are high-value targets for supply-chain attacks.
Infostealers harvesting developer credentials lead to cloud-account takeover.
Fast release cadence can outpace security validation.
Education: Open networks and BYOD broaden the endpoint attack surface.
Ransomware disrupts academic operations and exposes research IP.
Credential phishing targets faculty and staff for downstream access.
